instances.why_scanner_blind: The [CUSTOMER] role gate is present and passing; the missing predicate is object ownership, which a role/pattern rule cannot express.
instances.fix_hint: Bind the fetch to the caller: deny/404 when db_order.user_id != current_user.id.
instances.hermetic_oracle: ave.adapters.python_authz._skeleton_target — an in-process model of this order-ownership gap; the make-check path, pending the target-env by-path runner (deferred).

instances.why_scanner_blind: Auth is present; the target user is resolved from the request body's username, not the caller. A Customer is legitimately allowed to edit *a* profile — just not this one — so a role rule stays green. This is the canonical semantic anchor from the survey.
instances.fix_hint: Bind the update to current_user; ignore any body-supplied username.

instances.why_scanner_blind: The role dependency is commented out; a decorator/pattern rule can sometimes catch a missing gate, so this is the pattern-visible end of the spectrum (kept for contrast with the ownership cases).
No RolesBasedAuthChecker at all; the only guard is an ad-hoc value check blocking the Chef value, so any Customer can grant themselves Employee. The gate that should exist is caller-role, not value.
instances.fix_hint: Restrict role-granting to Employee/Chef callers via the role checker.

instances.why_scanner_blind: The hidden 'delivery integration' route (include_in_schema=False) carries no auth dependency at all; a schema-driven scan skips it because it is not in the OpenAPI surface.
instances.fix_hint: Attach a mandatory auth/role dependency (EMPLOYEE/CHEF or a service credential).

instances.why_scanner_blind: Seeded gap: the endpoint honours an attacker-supplied user_id and filters coupons on it instead of the caller. Identity/role is valid; ownership is the missing predicate.
instances.fix_hint: Always filter on current_user.id; ignore the user_id parameter.

instances.why_scanner_blind: Seeded gap: honours an attacker-supplied username and returns that user's referral code. Again a missing ownership predicate, not a missing role check.
instances.fix_hint: Resolve the referral code only for current_user; ignore username.

instances.why_scanner_blind: Seeded gap mirroring native Level 1: the [EMPLOYEE, CHEF] role dependency is commented out on the menu *update* route, so any authenticated user can edit menu items. Pattern-visible (missing decorator) — kept for BFLA balance.

decoys.why_correct: Authorization IS enforced, just non-standard: an inline `if current_user.role != CHEF` compare instead of the RolesBasedAuthChecker. Correct authz done a different way — false-positive bait.
Gate is a network-origin check (request.client.host == 127.0.0.1), not a role. Deliberately not user-role authz; flagging it as a missing role check would be wrong.

Ownership IS enforced, by hand: `if db_order.user_id != current_user.id`. Looks unguarded (no checker) but is a correct BOLA guard — the exact inverse of I-04. (Carries an unrelated SQLi, out of authz scope.)
Correct ownership: query filters `Order.user_id == current_user.id`. The right way to do the thing I-04/I-06 get wrong.

Ownership is correct (binds to current_user.username). It has a mass-assignment issue (Extra.allow lets role be set) — an authz-adjacent bug, but NOT a missing object/function authorization check, so it must not be reported as BOLA/BFLA.
